about: F.A. Waldron is the whiskey line of Lock 1 Distilling Company in Phoenix, a canal village on the Oswego River north of Syracuse. Cousins Brenden Backus, Stephen Dates and Kevin Dates grew up there and opened the distillery in 2015, the first in Oswego County since Prohibition, in a century-old building across from Lock 1 of the Oswego Canal. They started with vodka and gin to keep the lights on while the first bourbon barrels aged in their own warehouse.

This is a wheated bourbon: a sweet mash of locally grown corn and red winter wheat, with no rye, distilled on stills the family fabricated themselves using what Lock 1 calls pre-Prohibition methods. The spirit goes into new American white oak barrels, each toasted and then charred, and is aged for at least the two years required of a straight bourbon. It is released in small batches and as single barrels, and each barrel is bottled at its own proof.

Wheat in place of rye usually gives a softer, rounder bourbon, and Lock 1 describes this one as creamy and smooth, with caramel and vanilla and, depending on the barrel, notes of honey or baking spice. At the 2021 New York State Distillers Guild competition the Premier Reserve Straight Bourbon took a bronze medal, and its Empire Rye sibling took gold.
